density_challenge: The opposite case is that this unit is not yet standalone and should be held back or merged. First, the readable evidence is thin for the weight placed on it. Only seven full pages are readable (pp.42-44, 46, 50, 55-56) out of the 42-page Status chapter. Pp.47-49 and 51-54 are missing, and every accept/block claim rests on 2-3 line OCR snippets, so the second half has no full read at all. Second, the Palantir half stands on one witness. Qureshi's one-sentence reason ('breaks down social behavior mechanistically') and his body examples carry the Palantir link. Half of those examples cannot be found in the book, and 'casting' is unresolved, so the unit is mostly about Impro and says little about Palantir. Third, the evidence is Johnstone describing his own classroom with no measurement. He hedges it himself ('My belief (at this moment)') and admits that status is hard to perceive (p.42). The mechanisms that look strongest, such as the head-still chain and 'crutches', are his own teaching tricks. The accept/block half is contested by Johnstone himself: in 2007 he called 'accept all offers' a 'perversion', and the 2017 Theatre Museum interview on 'Yes, and' (Part 18) was not read, so a script that treats accept/block as settled could be wrong. Finally, this check found nine of the 61 Chinese statements overreaching and two with wrong locators, from small shifts of subject or attribution. Examples are Bion the therapist read as a teacher, the omitted 'low status' on p.50, the 'Excrement' cue, and the Globe's narration credited to McKinney. The explorer's source reading was solid, but the Chinese statement layer needed rework before it could be called ready. My own view is that the verdict holds for the Status half, narrowed to pp.42-46, 50 and 55-56, but accept/block should be a short second beat or a cut until the fuller sources below are read.
